summary.headline: GPT Healthcare Q1 FY27: revenue INR126.2 crore, EBITDA margin 20.4%, PAT up 66% YoY to INR12.7 crore; targets ~21% FY27 EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Total income rose 18.2% YoY and PAT rose 66% in Q1 FY27, with network occupancy at 45.5% and ARPOB at INR42,350. Mature-hospital occupancy excluding Raipur was 58.07%, and ~90% of revenue came from cash and insurance patients. Growth was attributed mainly to case-mix shift toward cardiology, oncology and neurosciences rather than tariff hikes, which come each October. Raipur losses were INR3 crore in Q1, and Jamshedpur (155 beds) is slated for Q4 FY27 commissioning, with a seventh hospital under evaluation to take capacity above 1,000 beds in two years.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26 also INR3 crore loss

segments.name: ILS Hospital Salt Lake
segments.commentary: Occupancy 62% (vs 60% YoY), ARPOB INR45,300 on higher-contribution surgeries; robotic procedures cumulatively above 800.

segments.name: ILS Hospitals Dumdum
segments.commentary: Occupancy 65% (vs 60% last year), ARPOB INR43,041; cardiac surgery started with ~200 surgeries in 5 months; renal transplants above 700.

segments.name: ILS Hospital Agartala
segments.commentary: Occupancy dipped slightly (ALOS cut from ~3.38 to 3 days, plus Tripura tribal-election movement curbs); ARPOB up 70% to INR41,573. Management cited last month's occupancy at ~51%.

segments.name: ILS Hospital Howrah
segments.commentary: Revenue up 31% YoY and occupancy up 16%; MAKO robotic knee replacement programme driving higher-complexity ARPOB.

segments.name: ILS Hospital Raipur
segments.commentary: Occupancy 17% vs 7% a year ago; ARPOB fell from ~INR44,500 in Q4 to INR42,300 due to Ayushman Bharat patient mix. Q1 loss INR3 crore; expected operational breakeven around 20 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected at ~21% vs 19% in FY26 (+200 bps); management put FY27 EBITDA at roughly INR110-115 crore, including other income.
Raipur loss expected to taper through the year; year-end occupancy target ~30%.

Jamshedpur (155 beds) to be commissioned in late Q4 FY27, subject to approvals; could slip to early next year. Expected ARPOB INR38,000-40,000 initially, converging toward Kolkata's ~INR42,000-43,000.
Jamshedpur breakeven in ~24 months; Dumdum and Howrah historically broke even within 12 months.
Dumdum expected to reach optimum occupancy this year and normalise around 70% by Q3 FY27.
Agartala expected to return to pre-disruption international patient levels in about 6 months; year-end occupancy target reaffirmed.
Long-term ROE and ROCE target of around 25%. Annual tariff increase each October, inflation-linked, a small contributor to ARPOB growth.
Management declined to give medium-term occupancy or mature-hospital revenue guidance for now; deferred to MUFG.
capex_capacity: Jamshedpur: 155-bed tertiary hospital under construction, on schedule for Q4 FY27; developer-built asset-light model on long-term rent (rent in the mid-30s INR crore, per management).
Raipur: asset-light model (developer-built building on long-term rent, same as Jamshedpur); ~10 liver transplants per year expected in first year.
Incoming debt of ~INR25 crore for Jamshedpur in FY27; overall debt unchanged YoY.

Seventh hospital under evaluation in Tier 1/Tier 2 eastern and central cities (Cuttack, Ranchi, Patna, Varanasi, Prayagraj), via greenfield or acquisition; target network capacity above 1,000 beds within 2 years.
Recently added: Dumdum cardiothoracic and vascular surgery unit; Howrah MAKO robotic knee programme; Agartala PET-CT and linear accelerator cancer centre (700+ radiation procedures).
demand_pricing: No tariff increase in Q1; ARPOB gains attributed to case-mix and specialty-mix shift. Management said 50-60% of ARPOB increase comes from mix.
Raipur ARPOB dip reflects limited Ayushman Bharat patient intake; management expects ARPOB to hold or rise now that most insurance empanelment is complete.
Government/scheme patients deliberately not pursued in Kolkata due to delayed payments and lower ARPOB.
Attrition: doctors ~6-7% in Calcutta, ~10% in Agartala and Raipur.
Bangladesh medical inflows at Agartala improved on targeted visa policy changes but still below pre-disruption levels.
Howrah: first corporate hospital in its micro-market; growth driven by awareness and consultant additions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Agartala occupancy fall, and is the year-end target intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy fell due to shorter ALOS (3.38 to 3 days, deliberate) and Tripura tribal-election movement curbs in May. Management said last month occupancy was ~51%, and the year-end target is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Raipur loss and ARPOB trajectory on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 loss was INR3 crore, expected to taper. ARPOB fell to INR42,300 from ~INR44,500 on Ayushman Bharat mix; exit occupancy target ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ARPOB rise sustainable, and is it price-led?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff hike in Q1; gains from case mix toward high-end tertiary care. Management hopes it continues and expects Dumdum and Salt Lake ARPOB to rise or hold.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company guide medium-term on occupancy and revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred this to MUFG (IR) with no specific guidance given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 EBITDA run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~21% FY27 EBITDA margin (vs 19% FY26), implying INR110-115 crore including other income.

risks_watch: Jamshedpur commissioning depends on approvals; slippage risk to early FY28.
Raipur ARPOB dilution from Ayushman Bharat volumes, and breakeven timing (~20 months).
Agartala dependence on Bangladesh inflows and regional disruptions; occupancy dipped in Q1.
Doctor attrition at 10% in Agartala and Raipur versus 6-7% in Calcutta.
Lease-based asset-light model implies rent of mid-30s INR crore per hospital, a fixed cost to monitor against ROCE.
Seventh hospital timing and deal terms (greenfield or acquisition) remain undisclosed.
key_quotes: We expect to close the year at around 21% EBITDA margins compared to the 19% of last year.
We'll request MUFG to get back to you on that.
We are not fixated on that model. This model has been successful for us in Raipur and in Jamshedpur.
We are assuming the ARPOB to increase, if not stay stable.
So, there has been -- the change is an evolution is a process, which is constantly happening. It is not something which finishes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural demand, ARPOB mix shift and the FY27 margin path, with a 21% EBITDA margin target and Jamshedpur on schedule. Cautious and deflecting on Agartala occupancy (ALOS cut, election curbs), Raipur ramp timing and Jamshedpur approvals, and declined medium-term occupancy or revenue guidance, deferring it to MUFG.
